definitions.explanation: Running over a long distance at a steady pace to test or build stamina. Commonly used in Japanese school physical education classes as a standard fitness activity.

examples.japanese: {持久走|じきゅうそう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧だ。
examples.english: I'm not good at long-distance running.

examples.japanese: ⟦{体育|たいいく}→体育：03384_taiiku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{持久走|じきゅうそう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We did an endurance run in PE class.

examples.japanese: ⟦{冬|ふゆ}→冬：00623_fuyu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{持久走|じきゅうそう}⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: In winter, schools hold endurance-running competitions.

examples.japanese: {持久走|じきゅうそう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{体力|たいりょく}→体力：05318_tairyoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ついてくる。
examples.english: If you keep doing endurance running, you build up stamina.

notes:
Composed of {持久|じきゅう} (endurance, lasting) + {走|そう} (running). Refers specifically to long-distance running as a form of exercise or fitness testing. In Japanese schools, {持久走|じきゅうそう} is a staple of winter PE classes, often culminating in a {持久走|じきゅうそう}⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧ (endurance-running competition) where students run distances from 1 km up to several kilometers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {持久走|じきゅうそう}⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧: endurance-run competition
- {持久走|じきゅうそう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧: bad at endurance running
- {持久走|じきゅうそう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to do endurance running
- {持久走|じきゅうそう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧: endurance-running practice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦マラソン→マラソン：04732_marason⟧: marathon — technically a specific 42.195 km race, but used loosely in Japanese for any long-distance run
- {長距離走|ちょうきょりそう}: long-distance running — the formal athletic-event term
- ⟦ジョギング→ジョギング：04738_jogingu⟧: jogging — more casual, for fitness at a relaxed pace

CULTURAL NOTE:
{持久走|じきゅうそう}⟦{大会|たいかい}→大会：03386_taikai⟧ is a well-known Japanese school event, often associated with cold winter weather and mixed feelings among students — seen as tough training but also a rite of passage.
